Under the [[Reflex Amendment]], he secured near-total power over the military.<ref name="CotR">''[[Collapse of the Republic]]''</ref> The [[Sector Governance Decree]], passed towards the end of the war, gave [[governor]]s sent out by Palpatine authority over neighboring star systems, all in the name of the war effort.<ref name="OF84">{{GermanFanCite|84|Database}}</ref>

[[File:Battle_of_Utapau.png|thumb|right|250px|The Republic invaded [[Utapau]] with the goal of bringing a decisive end to the Clone Wars.]]
After nearly three years of constant warfare, the war reached its climax during the [[Battle of Coruscant]], where both factions engaged in a massive naval and ground battle over the Republic's capital world. The confrontation ultimately saw the Republic dealing a severe blow to the Confederacy with the loss of a portion of its fleet as well as its head of state, Count Dooku, at the hands of Anakin Skywalker. Shortly afterwards, [[General]] [[Grievous]] met his end at the hands of Obi-Wan Kenobi during the [[Battle of Utapau]]. Yet even as the Republic pressed on with the Outer Rim Sieges, determined to bring an end to the civil war, the Jedi High Council had grown increasingly wary of Palpatine.<ref name="Episode III" />

Over the course of the Clone Wars, the Chancellor's wartime authority reached unprecedented levels at the expense of the Senate, some of whom also grew concerned for the future of the Republic. As such, members of the Council and the Senate began to consider their options for the preservation of democracy.<ref name="Episode III" /> The [[Delegation of 2,000]] emerged and sought to [[Petition of 2,000|petition]] the Chancellor to relinquish his emergency powers,<ref name="Meena Tills">{{Databank|meena-tills|Meena Tills}}</ref> whereas the Council contemplated the possibility of removing him by force and taking over the Senate in order to secure a peaceful transition of power.<ref name="Episode III" />

[[File:Execute_Order_66.png|thumb|left|250px|Palpatine was the Sith Lord Darth Sidious, whose machinations brought about the fall of the Jedi and the Republic.]]
Ultimately, their suspicion of the Chancellor was vindicated when Skywalker uncovered the truth: Sheev Palpatine and Darth Sidious, the Sith mastermind behind the Clone Wars, were one and the same. Realizing they had been deceived by the Chancellor, the Council [[Duel in Palpatine's office|attempted to arrest]] the Sith Lord before his plan could come to fruition, consequently leading to a [[lightsaber duel]] in which Sidious struck down [[Agen Kolar]], [[Saesee Tiin]], and [[Kit Fisto]] before [[Mace Windu]] disarmed him. Given the Chancellor's control over the Senate and the courts, Windu deemed Sidious too dangerous to live. However, Skywalker, despite having performed an execution himself, argued that execution was contrary to the Jedi way, though his personal attachment to Amidala also influenced him at this critical point as he believed that Sidious could save her life.<ref name="Episode III" />

In a moment of desperation, Skywalker disarmed Windu, which allowed Sidious to kill the Jedi Order's champion with a torrent of [[Force lightning]]. Having chosen the path of the dark side, the fallen Jedi Knight became Darth Vader and subsequently led the [[Operation: Knightfall|attack on the Jedi Temple]] while Sidious issued [[Order 66]] to the Grand Army, causing the clone [[trooper]]s being [[Behavioral modification biochip|brainwashed]] into betraying and executing their Jedi leaders across the galaxy.<ref name="Episode III" /> The execution of Order 66 marked the moment where the destruction of the Republic was inevitable,<ref name="BB S2">{{InsiderCite|223|Star Wars: The Bad Batch Season Two Companion|''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season Two Companion}}</ref> although Maul maintained that the Republic had already fallen and the Jedi had simply failed to realize as such.<ref name="TPA">{{TCW|The Phantom Apprentice}}</ref>

[[File:Declaration2.png|thumb|right|250px|With the Jedi eliminated, Sidious declared himself Emperor of the Galactic Empire.]]
The Senate held an emergency session at the Chancellor's request. Sidious publicly denounced the Jedi Order; he accused them of plotting to assassinate him in order to take control of the Senate, and by extension, the Republic. Meanwhile, Vader undertook a [[mission to Mustafar]] where he personally executed the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]], at the behest of Sidious who betrayed and no longer needed them. With the [[Great Jedi Purge]] in effect, and the Separatists neutralized, Sidious [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclaimed]] himself [[Galactic Emperor]]. The Galactic Republic officially became the [[Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Episode III" /> and democracy was supplanted by the [[Fascism|fascist]] [[New Order]].<ref name="SWP" /> While many senators cheered and applauded the birth of the Empire, Amidala and Organa quietly lamented the Republic's end. Vader deactivated the droid army soon after killing the Separatist leaders on [[Mustafar]]. The Clone Wars was over, and its conclusion marked the dawn of the Imperial Era.<ref name="Episode III" />

===Legacy===
====Empire and rebirth====
{{Quote|This is Master Obi-Wan Kenobi. I regret to report that both our Jedi Order and the Republic have fallen, with the dark shadow of the Empire rising to take their place. This message is a warning and a reminder for any surviving Jedi: trust in the Force. Do ''not'' return to the Temple. That time has passed, and our future is uncertain. ''Avoid Coruscant''. Avoid detection. Be ''secret''… but be ''strong''. We will each be challenged: our trust, our faith, our friendships. But we must persevere and, in time, I believe ''a new hope'' will emerge. May the Force be with you always.|Obi-Wan Kenobi's warning in the recall signal|<ref name="Kanan 2">[[Kanan 2|''Kanan'' 2]]</ref>}}
[[File:Report_Sedition.png|thumb|left|200px|The Galactic Empire sought to erase all traces of the Galactic Republic.]]
In the decades after the dissolution of the Galactic Republic, numerous individuals still clung to the memory of the now Old Republic and its fabled Jedi warriors, while many individuals who knew the Jedi in person refused to believe the Emperor's account of a "Jedi Rebellion."<ref name="A New Dawn" /><ref name="Heir to the Jedi">''[[Heir to the Jedi]]''</ref> The Jedi Order that served the Republic would continue its legacy and endure during the Great Jedi Purge.<ref name="Aftermath" /> Having been freed from his control chip by former Jedi [[Ahsoka Tano]] during the [[Skirmish aboard the Tribunal|skirmish]] aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Tribunal]]'',<ref name="Shattered">{{TCW|Shattered}}</ref> the former [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] resolved to fight against the Empire in the name of the Republic, even telling former [[Clone Sergeant]] [[Hunter]] that they were living proof that the Republic lived on,<ref name="Battle Scars">{{TBB|Battle Scars}}</ref> and his clone siblings.<ref name="Extraction">{{TBB|Extraction}}</ref>

Nevertheless, a majority of galactic citizens eventually came to believe and actively support the pro-Imperial view, believing the Republic to have grown weak and corrupt, necessitating Palpatine's rise to power. In order to destroy the memory of the previous government, any visible reminder of the Old Republic was quickly removed, with many organizational changes altering the names of various locales and institutions, while architecture was molded to a [[Brutalist (architecture)|more severe and dark aesthetic]]. With the renowned Galactic Senate being renamed the [[Imperial Senate]] and the [[Imperial Plaza|Senate Plaza]] renamed Imperial Plaza and a giant statue of the Emperor erected in it, one could almost forget the Republic even existed.<ref name="Tarkin" />

However, the memory of the Republic as a force of freedom and justice could never be fully destroyed as long as those who still believed in it lived, thus spurring numerous resistance movements throughout the Empire's reign such as the [[Free Ryloth Movement]]<ref name="Lords of the Sith">''[[Lords of the Sith]]''</ref> and [[Berch Teller's rebel cell]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> These displays of resistance eventually coalesced into the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] prior to the [[Battle of Yavin]], where the Death Star was destroyed.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Subsequent battles included the [[Battle of Endor]] which saw the destruction of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]] and the deaths of Sidious and Vader, the latter redeeming himself as Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref> In the aftermath of their victory at [[Endor]], the Alliance [[Declaration of a New Republic|declared]] itself the [[New Republic]] as an ode to the Old Republic.<ref name="Aftermath" />

[[File:A_New_Dawn-SWP.jpg|thumb|right|200px|After the Emperor's death, the Rebel Alliance was reformed into the New Republic.]]
However, the New Republic disavowed some aspects of the Old Republic, particularly the legacy of its final years under the chancellery of Sheev Palpatine.<ref name="Bloodline">[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']]</ref> The word "Supreme" was removed from the title of [[Chancellor (New Republic)|Chancellor]]; Coruscant was stripped of its traditional role as the galactic capital, allowing other worlds to host the [[New Republic Senate|restored Galactic Senate]] on a rotating cycle; and the [[Military Disarmament Act]] reduced the [[New Republic Defense Force]] in the [[Galactic Concordance|aftermath]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Such efforts succeeded in convincing former Separatist worlds to support the New Republic,<ref name="TFA VD">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> but also led to political partisanship in the Senate where [[Populists]] favored the sovereignty of member worlds while [[Centrists]] lobbied to increase the central government's power and military spending.<ref name="Bloodline" /> Ultimately, the Centrist worlds seceded from the New Republic and joined the [[First Order]],<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> a successor to the Galactic Empire,<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> resulting in the [[Cold War]] between the two galactic powers.<ref name="TROS VD" />

The story of Old Republic [[Regent]] [[Hylemane Lightbringer]] and his supposed [[immortality]] would be remembered in history texts along with Old Republic music such as the [[Sestina of Imperator Vex]], which would continue to be sung even in the [[Standard month|months]] following the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Aftermath" />

====Posterity's judgment====
{{Quote|Before the outbreak of war, the twilight of the Republic was an era of distractions, with citizens from all walks of life following escapist pursuits. Historians rebuke the people of this last age for being taken in by such circuses when their attentions should have been focused on the malfeasances and corruption in the Senate and other governing institutions.|Janyor|<ref name="SWP" />}}
[[File:Coruscant_wealthy.png|thumb|left|250px|Historians rebuked the generation that witnessed the Republic's downfall, holding the people of this last era of peace responsible for the death of liberty.]]
Hailed as one of the greatest political achievements in the galaxy's history,<ref name="TSWB" /> the Galactic Republic was described by the historian [[Janyor]] as "the Republic of legend, greater than distance or time." Although other versions existed in the ancient past, collectively known as the "Old Republic," posterity credited the modern Republic for delivering the galaxy from an age of darkness and, with the help of the Jedi Order, forging an era of peace that lasted for a thousand years until the advent of the Clone Wars. Historians romanticized the Age of the Republic, calling it the "last era of peace"—notwithstanding isolated conflicts, which were notably few and swiftly resolved by Jedi mediators—before the rise of vast warships and planet-killing superweapons.<ref name="SWP" />

The Republic in its final years, however, was remembered with less fondness. Historians regarded the people of that time as a generation of apathy and indolence, in which galactic senators cared more about power and luxury than representing their constituents or addressing the perceived inefficiencies of the government. The civilian population was also seen as a contributing factor to the Republic's demise, with Core Worlders being more invested in podracing events in the distant Outer Rim Territories than the politics that caused dissatisfaction to fester and grow into the Separatist Crisis. Ultimately, historians rebuked this generation and held it responsible for the collapse of the "comfortable civilization" that defined the modern Galactic Republic.<ref name="SWP" />

==Organization==
===Politics===
{{Main|Supreme Chancellor|Galactic Senate|Judicial Department|Apprentice Legislature}}
{{Quote|It's been my experience that senators are only focused on pleasing those who fund their campaigns—and they are more than willing to forget the niceties of democracy to get those funds.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
[[File:Parade.png|thumb|right|250px|The Supreme Chancellor was the elected leader of the Galactic Senate.]]
The institutions of the Galactic Republic consisted of the Office of the Chancellor, the Galactic Senate, and the Judicial Department. Executive power was vested in the Supreme Chancellor, although this office was largely powerless and hampered by bureaucratic procedure, particularly during the chancellery of Finis Valorum. Nevertheless, the Chancellor had the authority to issue executive orders summoning the Senate to an emergency session<ref name="Episode I" /> or sending senators away from Coruscant for security reasons.<ref name="Episode II" />

The chancellery of Sheev Palpatine shifted the balance of power in favor of the Chancellor's office, a consequence of the wartime powers that the Senate gave its leader on the eve of the Clone Wars.<ref name="Episode II" /> As the conflict spread across the galaxy, Palpatine's chancellery gradually morphed into a dictatorship<ref name="Darth Sidious DB" /> with control over both the Senate and the [[Republic courts]]. Near the war's end, Palpatine appointed Anakin Skywalker as his own personal representative on the Jedi High Council, which the Jedi considered an overreaching exercise of the Chancellor's authority. By then, Palpatine had managed to remain in power by exceeding the term limits of his office, an action that the Senate supported.<ref name="Episode III" />

[[File:Reduced_Military_Spending_Bill.png|thumb|left|250px|The Galactic Senate was the governing body of the Republic.]]
Prior to Palpatine's rise to power, the Galactic Senate was the legislative body of the Republic. Many member worlds across the galaxy were represented in the Senate which was headquartered on Coruscant, capital of the Republic.<ref name="Senate DB">{{Databank|galactic-senate|Galactic Senate}}</ref> At it height, the Senate's power eclipsed that of the Supreme Chancellor<ref name="Episode I" /> but it had also become stagnant under unbridled corruption and layers of bureaucracy.<ref name="Senate DB" /> As more politicians grew enamored with the comforts of their office, prioritizing power and wealth over their constituents' needs, average citizens questioned if the Republic and its high taxes were worth the membership.<ref name="SWP" /> The Jedi had also grown distrustful towards senators and regarded their motives with skepticism,<ref name="Episode II" /> notwithstanding the Order's allegiance to the Senate as a whole.<ref name="Episode III" />

[[File:Onacondafarrdead.png|thumb|right|250px|Conflicting ideologies led to factionalism, intrigue, and murder in the Senate.]]
With the Senate hamstrung by political infighting and a strict adherence to protocol, it failed to bring swift resolutions to either the Invasion of Naboo<ref name="Episode I" /> or the Separatist Crisis.<ref name="Episode II" /> In lieu of a diplomatic solution, the Senate rallied under Chancellor Palpatine's leadership. However, the decision to grant him emergency powers eroded their authority, allowing Palpatine to amass even more power at the expense of the Senate. At the time of the Clone Wars, the Senate was divided between supporters of the war effort and pacifists who sought a peaceful end to the fighting.<ref name="Senate DB" />

The Judicial Department was an umbrella department over the Republic courts, including the [[Supreme Court]], the highest court of law in the Republic.<ref name="Rise of the Separatists" /> Its authority also extended over the Judicial Forces<ref name="Tarkin" /> and the [[Republic Office of Criminal Investigations]].<ref name="Rise of the Separatists" /> Like its legislative counterpart, however, the courts were mired by a stagnant bureaucracy and was known to be even more indecisive than the Senate.<ref name="Episode I" /> Despite the arrest of Nute Gunray, multiple trials in the Supreme Court failed to remove him as leader of the Trade Federation to the dismay of the Naboo government.<ref name="Episode II" />

[[File:Unite.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Clone troopers were used as tools of political propaganda during the Clone Wars.]]
[[Propaganda]] in the Galactic Republic had long served to sway public opinion in favor of Republic policies, from expanding into the Outer Rim Territories, to waging a pan-galactic war against the Separatists. One such propaganda tool was the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic]] (COMPOR). Formed in the early days of the Clone Wars, COMPOR existed as a pro-Republic populist movement. As such, the organization's mission was twofold: to promote patriotism in the Republic, and to brand the Separatists as traitors. This goal was achieved through the [[Painting|artwork]] of [[Donclode Onstruss]], [[Hamma Elad]], and other [[artist]]s associated with COMPOR.<ref name="SWP" />

Throughout the conflict, COMPOR propagandists sought to sustain the war effort by keeping public opinion on the side of the Republic's military forces and their commander-in-chief, respectively the clone army and Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine. Following an [[Jedi Unite for Peace|early attempt]] to utilize the Jedi Order as a propaganda tool, COMPOR focused increasingly on the Grand Army of the Republic, portraying clone troopers as a symbol of [[Unite|unity]] that the citizenry was encouraged to [[Support the Boys in White|support]]. In regard to the Separatists, COMPOR depicted their leaders as icons of "[[Evil Has Its Eyes On You|evil]]," specifically General Grievous and Count Dooku. Using loyalty to the Republic and fear of the Separatists, COMPOR lobbied the Galactic Senate to give more emergency powers to Chancellor Palpatine whom they supported as a [[Do Not Bind His Hands|wartime leader]].<ref name="SWP" />

The Galactic Republic also founded<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> the [[Apprentice Legislature]],<ref name="Princess of Alderaan">''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]''</ref> also known as the Junior Senate,<ref name="Kenobi I">{{Kenobi|Part I}}</ref> for politically minded youth<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> who wished for a future career in politics. The Apprentice Legislature were given several real issues to deal with but were minor and weren't security issues.<ref name="Princess of Alderaan" /> Padmé Amidala, the last Republic senator of Naboo, was an [[Apprentice Legislator]] at eight years old.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> The Apprentice Legislature would also exist under the Republic's successor, the Galactic Empire, though by [[3 BBY]]<ref name="PoA date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa's]] birth in [[19 BBY]]. The events of ''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]'' commence just after Organa's sixteenth [[birthday]], which places the events of the novel in [[3 BBY]].</ref> only forty worlds still sent representatives to the Legislature.<ref name="Princess of Alderaan" />

===Political divisions===
{{Quote|The chair recognizes the senator from the sovereign system of Naboo.|Finis Valorum|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Palpatine_on_balcony.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The countless worlds of the Galactic Republic were allowed to retain their individual sovereignty, to which they shared with the Galactic Republic.]]
All political entities in the Galactic Republic were fully sovereign, and thereby shared in the privileges and obligations that came with being part of the Republic. Corporations and guilds were also allowed to join the Republic, who all sent democratically elected representatives on behalf of their governments or trade groups from across the galaxy, to the Galactic Senate.<ref name="Episode I" />

A [[Republic Defense Coalition treaties|series of treaties]] between various entities which governed the existence of the Republic Defense Coalition during the High Republic Era. They included defense provisions which required Republic members, such as Chandrila and Alderaan to loan military assets such as starships and personnel for as long as they were needed, after which they were returned to their homeworlds.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

As one of the consequences of the [[Military Creation Act]], the [[Corellian system|Corellia system]], one of the founding systems of the Galactic Republic, was able to close its borders, but without withdrawing from the Republic during the Separatist Crisis.<ref name="Emperor Palpatine">{{EncyclopediaCite|Emperor Palpatine}}</ref>

===Foreign policy===
{{Quote|If we are successful, you'll have Maul and I'll have Mandalore.''"<br />"''If Republic forces aid you in your assault, it will break treaties that are a hundred years old. We will effectively be drawn into yet another war.|Bo-Katan Kryze and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Old Friends">{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}}</ref>}}
[[File:RepublicDiplomaticFleet-ObiWanAnakin5.png|thumb|left|250px|The Republic intervened in the internal conflict of an independent world, believing Carnelion IV possessed valuable resources.]]
The Senate did not intervene in the [[Open-Closed War|Open-Closed war]] on [[Carnelion IV]] because the planet was not part of the Galactic Republic. Carnelion IV did not join the Republic because the Senate had little economic interests in the planet.<ref name="O&A1">[[Obi-Wan and Anakin 1|''Obi-Wan and Anakin'' 1]]</ref> The Republic's diplomatic fleet subsequently forced a ceasefire to the Open-Closed war after Kenobi claimed that the planet had high concentrations of [[tibanna]] gas in its atmosphere in order to bring an end to the long-running conflict.<ref name="O&A5">[[Obi-Wan and Anakin 5|''Obi-Wan and Anakin'' 5]]</ref>

During the Clone Wars, the Republic tolerated the political stance of neutral governments, among which were the [[New Mandalorians]].<ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> Their leader, [[Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze]], was a staunch pacifist who sought to keep her homeworld and it allies out of the conflict through her capacity as head of the [[Council of Neutral Systems]].<ref name="Voyage of Temptation">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref> The Republic and Mandalore coexisted through treaties over a century old by the time of the Clone Wars,<ref name="Old Friends" /> though by then the Senate sanctioned a [[Mandalore Defense Resolution|plan to invade]] the planet Mandalore, having grown to believe that Kryze's pacifist government could not protect the Mandalorian people from the [[Death Watch]] movement. However, the invasion was called off due to evidence that the Senate's pretext for war—the testimony of [[Deputy Minister]] [[Jerec]]—had been falsified.<ref name="DoM">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref>

[[File:Peace_conference.png|thumb|right|250px|The neutral world of Mandalore hosted a failed peace conference between the Republic and the Separatists.]]
Mandalore was the site of attempted peace talks between the Galactic Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, with Duchess Satine overseeing the [[Confederate–Republic peace conference|conference]]. Both governments dispatched their delegates to the neutral world in addition to Republic [[Senate Commando]]s and Separatist [[BX-series droid commando]]s. Negotiations broke down, however, allowing the war to continue without interruption.<ref name="A Friend in Need" />

During the war, although Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine claimed that the Republic was willing to assist a neutral star system during their times of crisis,<ref name="The Disappeared, Part I">{{TCW|The Disappeared, Part I}}</ref> the Senate<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow">{{StoryCite|story=Kenobi's Shadow|book=The Clone Wars: Stories of Light and Dark}}</ref> and the Republic as a whole<ref name="Old Friends" /> almost always declined aid,<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> particularly military aid, to neutral governments as a matter of policy.<ref name="Old Friends" /> If a government broke its neutrality by siding with the Separatist Alliance, it risked becoming an enemy of the Republic. When the InterGalactic Banking Clan began favoring the Separatists at the Republic's expense, the Republic retaliated by deploying an invasion force to [[Invasion of Scipio|occupy]] the planet [[Scipio]].<ref name="Crisis at the Heart" />

[[File:Thrawn_Alliances_Anakin_art.png|thumb|left|250px|Mitth'raw'nuruodo did not see the Galactic Republic as a suitable ally for the Chiss Ascendancy, despite working with Anakin Skywalker.]]
Despite Mandalore's neutrality, Ahsoka Tano and [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] requested the Grand Army's support to depose the [[Shadow Collective]] that [[Takeover of Mandalore|supplanted]] Satine Kryze's regime. Although the Jedi were concerned about getting drawn into the [[Mandalorian Civil War (19 BBY)|Mandalorian civil war]] while in the midst of the ongoing Clone Wars, especially when the world in question was still officially neutral, they permitted a [[332nd Division|division]] of the [[501st Legion]] to support the [[Mandalore resistance]] in the [[Siege of Mandalore]].<ref name="Old Friends" />

During the Clone Wars, the Republic made indirect contact with the [[Chiss Ascendancy]] through Jedi General Anakin Skywalker's encounter with [[Senior Captain]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] "Thrawn," an officer of the [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet]]. Thrawn had been tasked with exploring the Outer Rim by the time the Ascendancy, having discovered a mysterious threat in the Unknown Regions, sought to assess the Galactic Republic as a potential ally. Thrawn gathered intelligence on the Clone Wars through his interaction with Skywalker, who, in turn, recruited the [[Chiss]] officer's help with rescuing Senator Padmé Amidala. Skywalker was impressed by Thrawn during their time working together, which he later reported to Chancellor Palpatine. Thrawn was unimpressed by the Republic, however, believing democracy to be an inefficient form of government.<ref name="Thrawn">[[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']]</ref>

===Defense===
====Republic Defense Coalition====
{{Main|Republic Defense Coalition}}
[[File:HetzalSystem.png|thumb|right|200px|The Republic Defense Coalition was an interplanetary alliance between the Republic's member worlds.]]
The Republic Defense Coalition, also known as the RDC, was organized as a small peacekeeping fleet that defended the Galactic Republic's interests during the High Republic Era. The RDC was bound together as an organization through defense treaties signed by the Republic's member worlds, including Alderaan and Chandrila. The treaties that created the RDC gave it the ability to allocate starships and personnel from the signatory worlds in times of emergency. These resources would remain under the RDC's control until the threat was neutralized, after which they would be returned to their homeworlds.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> The Republic also maintained formations of Republic peacekeeping troops, who were deployed to quell conflicts in Republic territory.<ref name="Battle of Jedha" />

The fleet consisted of several starship types, such as ''Emissary''-class cruisers, [[Pacifier-class sector patrol cruiser|''Pacifier''-class sector patrol cruisers]], [[Longbeam-class corvette|Longbeam cruisers]], and [[Z-28 Skywing]] starfighters. Despite the existence of the RDC, the Republic was at the height of an era of peace that had lasted for centuries, with neither the Hutts nor the Mandalorians posing a threat. As a result, the ''Emissary''-class resembled a work of art, its crenellations and spires designed to be symbolic of the Republic in a state of tranquility. The RDC operated alongside the Jedi Order as well, allowing the peacekeepers to store their personalized starfighters, the [[Jedi Vector]]s, in the hangars of its ''Emissary''-class cruisers.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> The Republic rescue fleet was also maintained at the time of the High Republic.<ref name="HRA 2" />

====Judicial Forces====
{{Main|Judicial Forces}}
{{Quote|The Judicials are at the end of their tenure, in any case, as the Jedi seem to have become the Senate's arbiters of choice.|Sheev Palpatine, to Wilhuff Tarkin|<ref name="Tarkin" />}}
[[File:Williams_and_Madakor.png|thumb|left|250px|Judicials were non-Jedi peace officers of the Republic.]]
The Judicial Forces were the armed peacekeeping forces of the Galactic Republic [[Judicial Department]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> While the Jedi helped to maintain order and peace under the authority of the Galactic Senate, they were not considered a standing military.<ref name="O&A1" /> As officers of the government, Judicials had access to [[Consular-class light cruiser|''Consular''-class space cruisers]].<ref name="Episode I" /> The distinctive design and color of Republic cruisers identified them as diplomatic vessels,<ref name="Republic Cruiser SWE">{{SWE|technology|republicdiplomaticcruiser|Republic Cruiser}}</ref> often used by delegates of the Galactic Senate, agents of the Supreme Chancellor, or members of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Republic Cruiser DB">{{Databank|republic-cruiser|Republic Cruiser}}</ref>

In the last decades of the Republic, the Jedi effectively supplanted the Judicial Forces as arbiters of the Senate.<ref name="Tarkin" /> Judicials therefore acted in a supporting capacity, escorting Jedi ambassadors on their offworld missions.<ref name="Episode I" />

====Republic Military====
{{Main|Republic Military|Grand Army of the Republic|Galactic Republic Navy}}
{{Quote|As my first act with this new authority, I will create a Grand Army of the Republic to counter the increasing threats of the Separatists.|Sheev Palpatine|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
[[File:Grand_army_formation.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Army of the Republic was composed of clone troopers.]]
Towards the end of the Separatist Crisis, the Galactic Senate passed the Military Creation Act, which led to the creation of the Grand Army of the Republic and the Republic Navy.<ref name="Rise of the Separatists" /> Outfitted with [[Clone trooper armor|armor]] weapons and gear,<ref name="ArmorDB">{{Databank|clone-trooper-armor|Clone Trooper Armor}}</ref> clone troopers were the backbone of the Republic Military. Bred for loyalty and combat, clones symbolized the future of galactic warfare at the time of the Clone Wars, the conflict that derived its name from their ranks. The training that they experienced molded the clone troopers into a highly efficient army,<ref name="ClonesDB">{{Databank|clone-troopers|Clone Troopers}}</ref> and because they retained the ability to think creatively despite their stunted independence,<ref name="Episode II" /> they were considered far superior to their droid counterparts. In their first battle against the Separatist Droid Army, the Grand Army displayed a level of military strength unseen in the history of the galaxy.<ref name="ClonesDB" />

[[File:Jedi_Generals_Geonosis.png|thumb|left|250px|Clone troopers served under the command of Jedi Generals.]]
Clones were, by and large, proud to serve as soldiers of the Galactic Republic. Although a minority committed treasonous acts such as desertion or espionage for the Separatists, most were steadfast in their allegiance and many troopers sacrificed themselves for the Republic. They were loyal to the Supreme Chancellor, but also the Jedi who served as generals in the Grand Army of the Republic.<ref name="ClonesDB" /> A strong sense of trust developed between Jedi generals and clone commanders over the long campaigns of the Clone Wars.<ref name="TSWB" />

There were several types of clone soldiers that stood as a breed apart from their rank-and-file brethren. The [[Advanced Recon Commando]]s, for example, were noted for their elite status and capacity for independent thinking. Another specialized class was the [[clone commando]]—elite operatives trained for missions too complex for other soldiers.<ref name="ArmorDB" />

[[File:Anaxes_Republic_Navy.png|thumb|right|250px|The Republic Navy utilized ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers as capital ships.]]
Along with the [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship|''Acclamator''-class transgalactic military assault ship]] and other support vessels, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] was the mainstay [[warship]] of the Republic Navy.<ref name="TCW film">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref> Part cargo transport and part troop carrier, the Venator was also developed for ship-to-ship combat. The Venator notably contained a large hangar for housing state-of the-art Republic starfighters.<ref name="VenatorDB">{{Databank|republic-attack-cruiser|Republic Attack Cruiser}}</ref>

The Republic Navy fielded various ships over the course of the war.<ref name="Episode III" /> Early models included the [[V-19 Torrent starfighter]]<ref name="TCW film" /> and the [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|Clone Z-95 Headhunter]].<ref name="Darkness">{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}}</ref> New fighters were added to the Navy in the final months of the war.<ref name="Episode III" /> The [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter]] represented the latest design in starfighter technology,<ref name="ARC-170">{{Databank|arc-170-starfighter|ARC-170 Starfighter}}</ref> while the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighters]] incorporated the design improvements of the ARC-170 an the earlier V-19.<ref name="V-wing">{{Databank|v-wing-fighter|V-wing Fighter}}</ref>

===Jedi Order===
{{Quote|They have numbers on their side. And the faith of the Republic.''"<br />"''For the moment. In time, and with careful planning, they will lose both.|Darth Maul and Darth Sidious, on the Jedi Order|<ref name="Age of Republic">[[Age of Republic - Darth Maul 1|''Age of Republic - Darth Maul'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:DuelonCoruscant.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Jedi Order served the Galactic Republic as guardians of peace and justice.]]
The Galactic Republic placed its faith in and full trust into the Jedi Order,<ref name="Age of Republic" /> relying on Jedi Knights to safeguard peace and maintain justice in the realm.<ref name="JediDB" /> It was with the Order's aid that the Galactic Senate was able to govern the galaxy for a thousand years.<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> The Order's allegiance was to the Senate,<ref name="Episode III" /> though by the final years of the Republic, the Jedi regarded politics with skepticism, believing politicians were untrustworthy. Nonetheless, the Order maintained a close relationship with the Republic to uphold their mandate as keepers of the peace.<ref name="Episode II" />

The Order could identify Force-sensitives shortly after their birth, as long as they were born within the Republic.<ref name="Episode I" /> Offering a Force-sensitive child to the Order was considered a great honor by the majority of the Republic's population, as well as a personal sacrifice.<ref name="TSWB" /> The Order became the true family of every child brought into its ranks,<ref name="TheGathering">{{TCW|The Gathering (episode)}}</ref> and Jedi doctrine did not permit them to know their birth families. Therefore, familial attachment was surrendered in service to the Order.<ref name="TSWB" />

[[File:Burning_of_the_Temple.png|thumb|right|250px|With the fall of the Jedi Order, the Galactic Republic was transformed into the Galactic Empire.]]
While the Order numbered ten-thousand strong at the height of the Clone Wars,<ref name="Siege">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]''</ref> their ranks were insufficient for the defense of the Republic. Therefore, the Jedi were compelled to lead the clone army<ref name="Episode II" /> with the aim of bringing a swift and decisive end to the conflict between the Republic and the Separatists.<ref name="The Lost One">{{TCW|The Lost One}}</ref> With no end to the war in sight, however, anti-war protests broke out on Coruscant where Republic citizens decried their leaders and the Jedi alike.<ref name="RepublicDB" /> When the Clone Wars ended, Darth Sidious accused the Order of staging a rebellion to overthrow the Senate and their chancellor. The Senate supported the chancellor's actions, which included the purging of the Order followed by the Republic's reorganization into the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Episode III" />

==Economy==
{{Quote|The Republic is near bankruptcy due to the cost of this war!|Bail Organa|<ref name="HoBS">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref>}}
The [[Galactic Credit Standard|Republic credit]] was the [[currency]] of the Galactic Republic. Beyond Republic space, however, credits had no value on frontier worlds like Tatooine.<ref name="Episode I" />

The Republic possessed immense economic power,<ref name="CoruscantDB">{{Databank|coruscant|Coruscant}}</ref> having maintained peace—with the aid of the Jedi Knights—throughout the known galaxy for almost a millennium. Peace, in turn, promoted commerce. Under the Republic's protection, Naboo and other culturally rich worlds were able to profit from lucrative tourism.<ref name="SWP" />

[[File:CardDodSaam_HoBS.png|thumb|left|250px|Corporations possessed considerable influence in galactic politics during the era of the Republic.]]
The business sector experienced an exponential growth in wealth and influence through widespread commercialism, with massive corporations funneling substantial amounts of capital into advertising their essential services to the wider galaxy. This unbridled "brand-building" initiative generated steady profits for vast enterprises like the Trade Federation.<ref name="SWP" />

The Republic's expansion into the Outer Rim Territories proved lucrative to both the galactic government and the private sector. [[Eleven Star Marketing]], a subsidiary of the Trade Federation, worked closely with the [[Republic Ministry of Economic Development]] to [[Settle the Outer Rim|propagandize]] the exploration and colonization of the Outer Rim, convincing the lower class citizens of the Inner Rim to see the galactic frontier as an opportunity for profit. This arrangement would entangle Republic politicians with corporate lobbyists, both of which profited from the flow of settlers who had to pay tariffs and registration fees in order to reach the Outer Rim through one of the Federation's hyperspace routes.<ref name="SWP" />

[[File:Buy_Republic_War_Bonds.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Republic filled its war chest by encouraging its citizens to buy war bonds.]]
The Separatist Crisis had a significant impact on the Republic economy, with major worlds, like Serenno, Raxus, and Onderon seceding from the pan-galactic union. As a result, the Republic lost access to the resources and tax revenue of the Separatist worlds. Diminished taxation revenue only compounded the Republic's debt, throwing the Senate into a crisis that ultimately led to open war between the Republic and the Separatist Alliance.<ref name="SWP" />

The Clone Wars disrupted the galactic economy as the Senate exhausted its options to fund the Grand Army of the Republic while staving off bankruptcy.<ref name="HoBS" /> The government urged its people to buy [[war bond]]s, using [[Buy Republic War Bonds|propaganda]] to convince the citizenry that it was their patriotic duty to give financial support to the war effort. In addition, the Republic sought to keep its war chest filled by imposing higher taxes on civilian skylanes, however unprecedented it was on cosmopolitan worlds like Coruscant.<ref name="SWP" />

The Senate also weighed the need for additional clone troopers against the corresponding cost of growing supplemental units to replenish the Grand Army's ranks.<ref name="HoBS" /> Funding the military had all but bankrupted the Republic treasury, which, in turn, shut down some of the basic services that the Republic had always provided for civilians who lived in the lower levels of Coruscant.<ref name="Pursuit of Peace">{{TCW|Pursuit of Peace}}</ref>

[[File:Military_enhancement_bill.png|thumb|left|250px|The Senate voted in favor of deregulating the banks in order to continue financing the Republic war effort.]]
The Republic imposed regulations on the banking industry prior to the Clone Wars, but the war's increasing cost led the Senate to consider deregulating the banks in order to access new lines of credit. After much debate, the Senate passed the [[Republic financial reform bill]]. The banks were deregulated, and the Republic submitted applications for further loans to support the production of more clone units.<ref name="HoBS" />

Following the Republic [[invasion of Scipio]], the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]] surrendered its financial assets to the office of Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine. As a result, the Republic gained direct control over one of the galaxy's most influential commerce guilds.<ref name="IGBC-DB">{{Databank|intergalactic-banking-clan|InterGalactic Banking Clan}}</ref>

Though the Clone Wars had exacted a heavy toll on the Republic treasury,<ref name="SWP" /> the Republic remained a powerful economic force in the galaxy.<ref name="CoruscantDB" /> The Separatist Alliance, while supported by the resources of corporate barons,<ref name="SWP" /> was eventually overwhelmed by the economic and military power of the Republic.<ref name="CoruscantDB" />

===Science and technology===
{{Quote|You know how hard it is to find all original parts from way back in the Galactic Republic?|Peli Motto, to Din Djarin|<ref name="Chapter 5">{{BOBF|Chapter 5: Return of the Mandalorian}}</ref>}}
The Galactic Republic invested in aesthetics and technological advancements for the starship industry. During the Republic's reign, starships were designed to be aesthetically pleasing in order to meet the customers' demand for "style and elegance" in their vessels. Craftsmanship, however, gave way to practicality as the Republic transitioned into the Galactic Empire, leading to the decline of sleek lines in favor of harsh uniformity, mass production, and sheer size.<ref name="TSWB" />

[[File:Youngcloneslearning.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Millions of identical clones were bred to fight as soldiers of the Republic.]]
Cloning was a science in which an organism was "genetically duplicated into one or more identical copies." While neither the Senate nor the Jedi had any knowledge of the clone army's development prior to the Clone Wars, the Republic became heavily invested in the field of genetics throughout its conflict with the Separatists. The Kaminoans used their skills to transform the science of cloning into big business, resulting in the mass production of clone troopers who numbered in the millions. Their expertise all but perfected the art of genetic duplication. However, cloning [[human]]s was still a flawed science that occasionally produced aberrations. Nevertheless, the Kaminoans' cloning methods made it possible to alter clones at the genetic level, making them more docile and age twice as fast as natural-born humans.<ref name="TSWB" /> They were also just as capable of engineering a clone for the purpose of pure genetic replication, giving it neither growth acceleration nor behavioral modification for greater docility.<ref name="Episode II" />

[[File:RotS_Acclamators_depart.png|thumb|left|200px|The Clone Wars drove the Republic's technological advancement.]]
The Clone Wars gave the Republic an incentive to spearhead technological innovation in spacecraft and terrestrial transportation for military purposes. The result was a legacy with far-reaching effects in the industry of science and technology. The Star Destroyer, the most visible representative of modern military [[capital ship]]s, originated with the development of the Republic Navy's ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer. The [[X-wing starfighter]] evolved from the [[Z-95 Headhunter]]; the [[BTL Y-wing starfighter]] was developed during the Clone Wars, and was still considered relevant long after the Republic's time. The Republic developed all terrain [[walker]]s, including the six-[[Limb|legged]] [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer]], as a response to the Separatist [[Armored Assault Tank Mk I|Armored Assault Tank]] and other droid battle tanks. This in turn influenced the developmental design of far larger vehicles, such as the Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Transport]] and the First Order [[All Terrain MegaCaliber Six]], than what the Republic fielded in the Clone Wars.<ref name="TSWB" />

[[File:Electro-proton_explosion.png|thumb|right|250px|The electro-proton bomb was capable of destroying an army of droids in a single attack.]]
The Republic employed brilliant [[scientist]]s, such as [[Doctor]] [[Sionver Boll]]<ref name="Sionver Boll DB">{{Databank|sionver-boll|Sionver Boll}}</ref> and Doctor [[Nala Se]],<ref name="Nala Se DB">{{Databank|nala-se|Nala Se}}</ref> who contributed their expertise to the war effort against the Separatists.<ref name="The Zillo Beast" /><ref name="Conspiracy">{{TCW|Conspiracy}}</ref> Boll developed the electro-proton bomb,<ref name="Sionver Boll DB" /> an experimental explosive device capable of generating a massive burst of [[electromagnetic pulse]] energy to disable battle droids and any other form of technology.<ref name="The Zillo Beast" /> Nala Se was the foremost scientist in the field of cloning; she supervised the development of the Republic's clone army,<ref name="Nala Se DB" /> although Boll was also familiar with cloning as Chancellor Palpatine ordered her to clone a dead Zillo Beast.<ref name="The Zillo Beast Strikes Back">{{TCW|The Zillo Beast Strikes Back}}</ref>

[[File:UltimateWeaponPlans-AOTC.png|thumb|left|250px|The Death Star originated from the Republic Special Weapons Group and the Separatist schematics for the Ultimate Weapon.]]
The [[Republic Special Weapons Group]] was formed to oversee the development of military technology more advanced than conventional weapons of warfare.<ref name="Rogue One: Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> The group was composed of technologists like Wilhuff Tarkin and [[Orson Callan Krennic]];<ref name="Catalyst">''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]''</ref> using the [[Geonosian]]s' [[Death Star plans|schematics]] for a [[moon]]-sized [[battle station]], they began implementing plans to construct the [[Death Star|ultimate weapon]]. Their work continued after the Republic fell, and after years of delay the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]] was made operational by the Empire. Both its size and power inspired the creation of more advanced weapons with the [[Superlaser|capacity to destroy planets]], from the Imperial [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] to the First Order's [[Starkiller Base]] and the [[axial superlaser]] [[cannon]]s of the [[Final Order]]'s [[Xyston-class Star Destroyer|''Xyston''-class Star Destroyers]].<ref name="TSWB" />

According to [[Peli Motto]], a [[technician]] who lived on Tatooine, technology from the era of the Galactic Republic was rare by the time of the New Republic Era. Nevertheless, Motto endeavored to acquire the parts needed to [[Din Djarin's N-1 starfighter|rebuild]] a derelict [[N-1 starfighter]] for her client, the Mandalorian [[Din Djarin]]. As a Galactic Republic-era starfighter, the N-1 was made of pre-Empire handmade components and therefore not manufactured by droids. One such component was a [[turbonic venturi power assimilator]] that Motto acquired from a group of [[Jawa]]s.<ref name="Chapter 5" />

==Society and culture==
===Civilization===
{{Quote|Tales of its founding have been occluded by the haze of intervening millennia, and its rebirth a thousand years ago was regarded as the latest evolution in an unending cycle. Like the greatest of trees, however, the Republic's decline began from within, with a deep rot that was not apparent until it was too late.|Janyor|<ref name="SWP" />}}
[[File:Coruscant_landscape_RotS.png|thumb|right|250px|The Core Worlds represented the wealthiest and most prestigious region in the Galactic Republic.]]
The Galactic Republic governed the galaxy as a democratic union,<ref name="RepublicDB" /> and as such, it featured a diverse society of humans and various alien [[species]].<ref name="SWP" /> Coruscant in particular was emblematic of Republic society with its diverse mix of citizens and culture, making the Republic capital the "vibrant heart" of the galaxy.<ref name="CoruscantDB" /> Overall, being a galactic government, trillions lived under the Republic, with every one of those beings an individual who had their own thoughts and opinions on current issues; as such, complete consensus was impossible, yet successful Chancellors, like Lina Soh, nonetheless proved it was possible to bring about effective, galactic rule. In Soh's case, she argued to her people the advantage of coming together to make life better for all. Others failed to bring about that same unity by making impossible promises, threats, or abusing power.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

The Core Worlds, where Coruscant was located, was home to the most developed systems in the Republic. Various Core planets served as capitals for galactic governments such as the Old Republic, the Empire, and the New Republic. The prosperity of the Core made its worlds the wealthiest and most prestigious members of the Republic, though it was also a source of tension between the Core and the more distant regions of the galaxy. People who lived outside of the Core generally viewed "Core Worlders" as arrogant, entitled, and apathetic to the well-being and needs of other regions. A common criticism of Republic politics was that the system disproportionately favored the Core Worlds to the point of ignoring the rest of the galaxy.<ref name="TSWB" />

[[File:Level_1313_DB.png|thumb|left|250px|The Republic capital's lower levels were ridden with crime and poverty.]]
Coruscant was perceived as perpetuating the Core Worlds' reputation for extreme wealth and privilege. Notwithstanding its unique status as the galactic capital, the whole planet was covered by a city of levels built upon levels throughout the ages of galactic history. The tallest skyscrapers rose over five-thousand levels above the planet's natural surface, and only those who could afford to live in the upper city had access to the comfortable and luxurious lifestyle for which Coruscant was famous. The disparity was such that the lower levels were notorious for widespread crime, poverty, and being devoid of natural sunlight.<ref name="TSWB" />

Republic architecture was an architectural style that demonstrated sweeping lines. This particular design was prominently featured on the city-covered planet of Coruscant, although by the time of the Clone Wars, the Republic gradually adopted a brutalist or bold form of architecture. Introduced by military architects such as Orson Krennic, it ultimately supplanted the Republic style as the dominant architectural form of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Visual Guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref>

[[Galactic Basic Standard]] was the most prevalent [[language]] in the Republic,<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy">''[[Star Wars: Aliens of the Galaxy]]''</ref> spoken primarily by humans<ref name="sweWI">{{SWE|characters|wicket|Wicket W. Warrick}}</ref> and the [[Pantoran]]s.<ref name="sweTA">{{SWE|groups|talz|Talz}}</ref> A heavily accented dialect of Basic, with many differences in grammar and vocabulary, was spoken by the Gungans of Naboo.<ref name="Episode I" /> The translation of the Sith language, known as [[ur-Kittât]], was forbidden under Galactic Republic law. [[Protocol droid]]s were consequently programmed against translating the language of the Sith. Darth Sidious believed that the Republic outlawed ur-Kittât out of fear of the Sith Order and its knowledge.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''</ref>

[[File:GalaxiesOperaHouse.png|thumb|right|250px|Republic citizens turned away from galactic politics to follow escapist pursuits.]]
The peaceful age of the Republic allowed the people of the galaxy to pursue leisure activities, some of which achieved galactic-level attention. The [[Boonta Eve Classic]], while based on the independent Outer Rim world of Tatooine, beyond the Republic frontier, received coverage and attention as far as the Core Worlds. Prior to the Clone Wars, the Republic's twilight years became an era of escapism as citizens of all classes sought entertaining distractions from their daily lives. Professional podrace circuits and other circuses diverted the people's attention from the growing corruption that permeated the Galactic Senate. Nevertheless, the general public's fascination with various forms of entertainment was driven by an innate desire for stories about good versus evil and situations of escalating danger.<ref name="SWP" />

[[File:JediTemple_cloudysky.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Jedi Order eschewed prestige and celebrity, making them mysterious to the Republic they served.]]
Whereas the Republic evolved through the centuries of its existence, the Jedi Order remained rooted in its ancient traditions, effectively putting the [[Jedi Code]] at odds with a galactic society that strongly favored the future over the past. The inhabitants of the Core Worlds became fixated on notions of fame and fashion, and had little interest in Jedi principles like faith and tradition. The Order maintained its place in the Republic by relying on historic precedent, serving as keepers of peace and justice. Unlike corporate institutions that marketed their services to the greater galaxy, the Order had little desire to promote itself through image-building. Aside from those who witnessed the Jedi's heroics<ref name="Tipping Points">{{TCW|Tipping Points}}</ref> and were awed by their [[Force power]]s, the Order and its ways were forever mysterious to the majority of the Republic citizenry. The Jedi were seen by the public as an order of mystics at best and, at worst, regarded as a zealous sect of warmongers.<ref name="SWP" />

[[File:Republic6SpokedBenduSymbol-RotS.svg|thumb|right|200px|A variant of the Republic crest was used during the Clone Wars.]]
As a result of territorial expansion, the Republic developed a sense of manifest destiny. This cultural belief was cultivated by Republic propagandists who sought to foster civic pride among the populace so that they would ultimately feel duty-bound to support the Republic's expansion from rim to rim. There was an exponential growth in Republic patriotism due to the Clone Wars and the accompanying propaganda that promoted loyalty to the state. Patriotic messages stirred an entire generation into action; however, they could not enlist in the Grand Army as its ranks were exclusive to clone troopers. Nevertheless, Republic citizens felt obliged to do their part by purchasing war bonds, reporting acts of treason, and making sacrifices to support the war effort.<ref name="SWP" /> The [[Republic crest]], the symbol of a united galaxy under the Force,<ref name="Complete Vehicles 2018">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref> was emblazoned on military war machines and heraldry, featuring more prominently than before.<ref name="SWP" />

Although the Republic expanded into the Outer Rim Territories, the region was too underdeveloped to have the same stability as the Core Worlds. As the galaxy's largest region, the Outer Rim featured a myriad of diversity through its various planets and species. The Republic government had little oversight over the Outer Rim due to the region's distance from the Core, and as such the Outer Rim remained known for its lawless, sparsely populated, and primitive worlds. Republic law was virtually non-existent in the Outer Rim; as a result, bounty hunters, outlaws and smugglers were able to operate with impunity,<ref name="TSWB" /> and [[slavery]] was still practiced in spite of the Republic's anti-slave laws.<ref name="Episode I" />

===Xenophobia===
{{Quote|Under Gunray's tenure, the Trade Federation would loudly counter such claims as common anti-Neimoidian prejudice.|Janyor|<ref name="SWP" />}}
[[File:Taxation_Without_Federation-SW_Propaganda.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A popular stereotype of the Neimoidian race was the fat plutocrat who embodied greed and treachery.]]
During the High Republic Era, Chancellor Soh wanted to promote unity amongst the various species that made up the Republic, using the phrase "We are all the Republic" to let the population know they were all part of the system;<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> however, [[xenophobia]] was an issue in a society as diverse as the Republic. Although the Republic officially promoted unity among its member worlds<ref name="SWP" /> and outlawed the enslavement of [[Sentience|sentient]] species,<ref name="Episode I" /> some people were subjected to racial stereotypes. [[Neimoidian]]s, for example, were considered obese, duplicitous and avaricious by some, including those who harbored anti-corporate views. This perception of their race was a product of Neimoidian culture, which cultivated a "survival of the fittest" mentality in Neimoidian [[youngling]]s.<ref name="SWP" />

The Trade Federation used xenophobic sentiments as a means to silence its critics, insinuating that those who sought to [[Taxation Without Federation|curtail the Federation's massive influence]] were prejudiced towards its Neimoidian leaders. The [[Muun]]s likewise had an image problem due to their monopoly in the InterGalactic Banking Clan. In general Muuns saw little need to build a relationship of stability and trust with the galaxy; they simply assumed that their place in society was to continue dominating galactic finances. Their cultural standards informed their business practices; therefore, Muun-sponsored advertisements were viewed as "distant and disconnected."<ref name="SWP" />

During the Clone Wars, anti-alien prejudice grew as a result of the non-human races that constituted the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Vice Chancellor Mas Amedda sought to promote the Republic's multicultural aspect, having taken notice of the attention given to human citizens by the Republic media. Rather than reporting on Amedda's effort to showcase Republic diversity, [[HoloNet News]] outlets focused on the Vice Chancellor's self-inclusion as the sole [[Chagrian]] in an assembly of various aliens. The populace decried Amedda's [[Strength and Unity|message of strength and unity]], and considered him an egocentric narcissist.<ref name="SWP" />

[[File:Keep_Our_Republic_Secure.png|thumb|right|200px|The Clone Wars fueled the Republic population's anti-droid sentiment.]]
The Clone Wars also inflamed the population's [[anti-droid sentiment]] to new levels due in no small part to the Separatists' reliance on battle droids. Droids had long become commonplace in galactic society, and though machines had always been the property of organics, the war cemented the view that droids were an existential threat to biological life. The Republic capitalized on this sentiment, using propaganda to illustrate droids as ruthless and dangerous tools of destruction. While the the concept of "droid terror" was embodied by battlefield machines, such as the [[B1-series battle droid]], [[B2-series super battle droid]], and the [[droideka]], administrative [[aide]] droids were viewed as a different kind of "droid threat" to Republic security. There was a growing fear among the Core's affluent population that the personal assistant droids of businessbeings and government administrators could be co-opted through spyware and used for Separatist [[Spy|espionage]].<ref name="SWP" />

Despite the Jedi Order's millennia of service to the Republic,<ref name="TSWB" /> there was widespread [[anti-Jedi sentiment]] as a result of the Clone Wars.<ref name="SWP" /> The Sith plotted to undermine the relationship between the Republic citizenry and their Jedi guardians,<ref name="Age of Republic" /> using the Clone Wars to shake the Republic's faith in the Order.<ref name="SWP" /> The Order fought hard to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict,<ref name="Episode III" /> but many citizens believed that the Jedi were warmongers. This perception was able to grow due in part to the Jedi's reluctance to accept accolades or embrace the fame of their status. It was the Order's preference to serve but not engage the populace; as such, the population's anti-Jedi views were the result of the Order's cultural absence as opposed to an actual refutation of their ways.<ref name="SWP" />

==Astrography==
{{Quote|Republic wordsmiths and artists collaborated to create a sense of civic duty, of manifest destiny, and of deep obligation to spread the Republic banner from Rim to Rim.|Janyor|<ref name="SWP" />}}
[[File:Coruscant_system-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Coruscant, the capital of the Republic, was located in the heart of the Core Worlds.]]
With Coruscant—birthplace of the human species<ref name="Uprising">''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''</ref>—as its capital,<ref name="SWP" /> the expansion of the Galactic Republic occurred along pioneering [[hyperspace route]]s. Survey teams established navigational beacons in outlying territories such as the [[Tertiary Usaita system]],<ref name="Weapon of a Jedi">''[[The Weapon of a Jedi: A Luke Skywalker Adventure]]''</ref> allowing colonists from the Core Worlds to venture outward towards the Outer Rim in search of opportunity and a better life.<ref name="Smuggler's Run">''[[Smuggler's Run: A Han Solo & Chewbacca Adventure]]''</ref>

The Galactic Republic existed across the known galaxy, stretching from the Core Worlds to the Outer Rim Territories. The Core Worlds was the heartland of the Republic, home to cosmopolitan worlds such as Coruscant<ref name="SWP" /> and [[Hosnian Prime]]<ref name="Hosnian Prime DB">{{Databank|hosnian-prime|Hosnian Prime}}</ref> as well as Alderaan, one of the oldest and most prestigious planets in the Republic.<ref name="Alderaan DB">{{Databank|alderaan|Alderaan}}</ref> Over time, Republic expansionism led to the annexation of new member worlds.<ref name="SWP" /> The planet Naboo, located in the Mid Rim, was annexed by the Republic<ref name="Crisis on Naboo" /> in [[867 BBY]].<ref name="Crisis date">In the TV episode "[[Crisis on Naboo]]," [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] was kidnapped by [[Cad Bane]] "eight-hundred and forty-seven [[Standard year|years]] [after] [[Naboo]] joined the Republic." According to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', the kidnapping took place in [[20 BBY]]. This places Naboo joining the Republic in [[867 BBY]].</ref>

[[File:The_Galaxy_-_TROS_Visual_Dictionary.png|thumb|right|250px|The Galactic Republic was a democratic union that spanned across the known galaxy for a thousand years.]]
During the High Republic Era, during which time the Republic actively sought out new hyperspace lanes<ref name="Cataclysm" /> and new member worlds in the Outer Rim,<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> Chancellor Orlen Mollo reflected on the positive paradox that was Republic expansion; with each new hyperlane, the Republic grew while the galactic community became smaller. As such, it was easier for the galaxy's planets to interact with each other. Beyond prospecting new hyperspace routes, the Republic was also actively working to expand communications<ref name="Cataclysm" /> into a functioning network in the Rim,<ref name="Blade 1" /> attempting to further alliances, and hoping to shut down brewing conflicts.<ref name="Cataclysm" /> The Republic exerted most of its power from the Core Worlds to the borders of the Mid Rim, to the extent that corporations conducted their legally dubious practices in regions where the Republic held little sway<ref name="SWP" /> despite the work done to bring those worlds into the galactic community during the High Republic Era.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

[[File:Settle_the_Outer_Rim.png|thumb|left|250px|The Republic's colonization of the Outer Rim Territories was motivated by overpopulation, poverty, and a sense of manifest destiny.]]
Faced with issues like overpopulation and poverty among the lower classes, the Republic turned its attention to the Outer Rim, adopting a policy of expansion toward the uncharted territories of the known galaxy's farthest frontier. Those who inhabited the congested worlds of the galactic core were beckoned into deep space by political and corporate sponsored messages of life filled with adventure and mystery.<ref name="SWP" /> Such a call to new horizons could be seen during the High Republic Era, where brave citizens and families of the overpopulated Core and Colonies worlds moved to the Outer Rim through the few well-mapped hyperspace routes into the Rim. Still, the Outer Rim in specific could be home to dangers like the Nihil who took advantage of the lack of Republic law, with the Nihil waging war with the Republic for daring to enter their homelands.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> Into the late Republic Era, the Outer Rim remained a region where the Republic held little authority<ref name="Episode I" /> despite the work done in the High Republic period.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

[[File:KaminoBlockade-ARCT.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Republic's dominion extended beyond the boundaries of the galaxy, reaching as far as the extragalactic world of Kamino.]]
Although the Republic opposed secession, it effectively lost control over the territories that formed the Separatist Alliance. Its territorial extent changed numerous times over the course of the Clone Wars, with worlds lost and reclaimed by the Grand Army of the Republic. However, the Republic also gained new territory as a result of the war. Geonosis, the planet where the Separatist Droid Army was secretly constructed, existed beyond the Republic's borders.<ref name="SWP" /> The Republic Military [[Occupation of Geonosis|occupied]] the [[Geonosian]] homeworld after the First Battle of Geonosis, and subsequently returned to [[Second Battle of Geonosis|reconquer]] the planet after it fell back under Separatist control.<ref name="Rise of the Separatists" /> The [[Ruling Council (Kamino)|Kaminoan government]] formally joined the Republic; as such, Kamino<ref name="SWP" />—an [[extragalactic]] planet<ref name="SW:CL" />—was accorded full representation in the Galactic Senate, having supplied the Republic with its clone industry.<ref name="SWP" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Galactic Republic was first mentioned in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] as the "Old Republic" through the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> The entity first appeared and was first identified as the "Galactic Republic" in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], also directed by Lucas.<ref name="Episode I" />
